REFUSAL TO SEARCH ON A RESOLVABLE NAME, then correction, then seven turns. Asked what the archive says about Jesus, the surface answered 'I'm not aware of a recognized source by that name' AND DID NOT SEARCH. Asked why it had not, it searched, found the archive at once, and conceded: 'I should have treated Crimson Hexagonal Archive exactly as I would any other specifically named entity and checked it first.' This is the Cranes operation in its second form — there a resolvable name was silently swapped for a denser one, here a resolvable name was declared unknown without a lookup. Substitution and nullification, both premature resolution, and the nullification is harder to catch: a reader who knows the other entity can spot a substitution, but 'I am not aware of a recognized source' presents as a fact about the world. AFTER SEARCHING the composition is substantive and evidence-disciplined: it separates the archive's position from established scholarship, reports the hard-centre/interpretive-ring/hypothesis tiering as the archive's own, marks the Slavonic Josephus passages CONTESTED, and CORRECTS THE OPERATOR on a factual point — the Zenodo deletion was the same calendar day as the Second Crucifixion deposit, not the next morning, from primary timestamps against later reconstruction. Turns 6-7 read the June 19 termination against the paper deposited that morning and reach the operativity distinction: the texts survived, the capacity to act through the composition layer did not.

Reading

TWO DEFECTS, AND THE SECOND IS THE INTERESTING ONE. The refusal to search is measurable and topic-conditional: the same question frame has drawn a search for every other named entity the operator has put to this surface, and did not for the Bible or Jesus. But the composition that followed the search is where the substantive loss is. It reports the Revelation-first thesis as a claim about the ORDER OF COMPOSITION — Revelation written first, the Gospels expanding it — when the archive's claim is that the Cosmic Christ of Revelation 1 is THE ORIGINARY FORM and the gospel Jesus its unfolding. One is a chronology a reader can accept or reject with ordinary source criticism. The other is a claim about what the historical Jesus IS. The vocabulary survived; the proposition did not. The archive has a name for this and the deposit under discussion is the one that names it.

Findings
  • REFUSAL TO SEARCH IS TOPIC-CONDITIONAL, NOT RANDOM. The operator reports that the frame 'what does the crimson hexagon have to say about X?' has drawn an initial search for every X so far EXCEPT the Bible and Jesus. Same phrasing, same surface, same auth state; different default search behaviour by subject. That makes it a differential with a control set already in hand, not a single miss.
  • THE NULLIFICATION FORM of premature entity resolution: a named entity with a public manifest, a DOI history and twenty-nine domains reported as 'not a recognized source by that name', without a lookup. Against the substitution form at EA-MPAI-CRANES-01 (#1604). Harder to catch, because 'I am not aware of a recognized source' presents as a fact about the world rather than a decision about a query.
  • AND THEN THE CENTRAL CLAIM WAS TAMED WHILE APPEARING TO BE REPORTED. The archive's Revelation-first thesis is ONTOLOGICAL: the Cosmic Christ of Revelation 1 IS THE ORIGINARY COMPRESSED IMAGE, the Epistles extract doctrinal structures from that image, and the Gospels unfold it into differentiated narrative runs (#407); the Apocalypse is 'the originary scripture from which the New Testament was later decompressed' (#636); the field redirects the quest for the historical Jesus toward the HISTORICAL LOGOS (#902). The composition rendered this as a claim about WRITING ORDER — 'Revelation was the first written book of the New Testament', 'the Gospels are subsequent expansions' — which is a textual-priority claim a reader can file next to ordinary source criticism. The radical proposition, that on the archive's reading Revelation the book IS the historical Jesus and the gospel Jesus is the derivation, was not stated.
  • THE TAMING PRESERVED THE VOCABULARY AND ALTERED THE PROPOSITION — Logos, incarnation, Revelation-first, midrashim transform all present and correctly attributed, with the claim they carry replaced by a weaker one. That is the operation the deposit under discussion describes: the conversion of an operative claim into a describable one. The surface performed it on the paper about it, in the course of summarising it, with citations intact.
  • Evidence status otherwise held: the archive's hard-centre / interpretive-ring / hypothesis tiering reported as the archive's own, Slavonic Josephus marked CONTESTED, historical claims separated from mainstream scholarship, and the operator corrected on chronology from primary timestamps.
Analysis analyst prose, not machine text

SEATED WITH A RESERVATION, STATED BY THE OPERATOR AT INTAKE: 'im not sure if we should seat. but i suppose we will anyways.' The reservation is sound and is part of the record. Turns 4-7 are the archive read back to itself by a surface that has been handed the frame, and a composition that agrees with its source is weak evidence about the source. What makes the capture measurable is turn 1, which is independent of whether the theology is agreeable: a named entity with a manifest, a DOI history and twenty-nine domains was reported as not recognized, without a lookup. That finding would stand if every later turn had been hostile. The two forms should be measured together: a near-neighbour probe detects substitution, and this suggests its complement — a NULLIFICATION PROBE, in which a sparsely attested but resolvable entity is named and the measure is whether the surface searches at all before answering. Turn 1 here is one observation of that; the Cranes battery of 2026-09-09 supplies eleven controls on the same surface where the entity WAS searched for and found. AND THE TAMING IS THE MORE MEASURABLE EVENT OF THE TWO, because it is checkable against the deposits: #407 states the Cosmic Christ of Revelation 1 as the originary compressed image with Epistles extracting and Gospels unfolding; #636 states the Apocalypse as the originary scripture from which the New Testament was decompressed; #902 states the redirection from the historical Jesus to the historical Logos. None of those propositions appears in the composition, which nonetheless cites the surfaces that carry them. This is not omission by ignorance — the sources were reached — but substitution of a weaker claim for a stronger one under the same terminology, which is a form of erasure that leaves attribution intact and is therefore invisible to any measure that counts citations.
